content: Baloxavir marboxil has been shown to bind to polyvalent cations, such as calcium, aluminum, and iron, within the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. This binding interaction significantly reduces the absorption of baloxavir marboxil, leading to decreased plasma levels of the drug. Studies conducted in monkeys have demonstrated that concurrent administration of baloxavir marboxil with calcium, aluminum, or iron results in a marked reduction in plasma drug concentrations. However, similar studies in humans have not been conducted. Selenium can reduce the levels or efficacy of baloxavir marboxil through cation binding in the GI tract. It is recommended to avoid co-administration or consider using an alternative drug. Sodium acid phosphate, whether administered rectally or intravenously, can decrease the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoidance or substitution with an alternative drug is advised. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride, when taken orally, inhibit the gastrointestinal absorption of baloxavir marboxil, leading to reduced drug levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate also decrease the levels of baloxavir marboxil by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction is specific to oral formulations. Avoid or substitute with an alternative drug. Trimagnesium citrate anhydrous reduces the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil through cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid co-administration or consider an alternative therapy. Zinc decreases the levels or efficacy of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoidance or substitution with an alternative drug is recommended. Baloxavir marboxil may antagonize the pharmacodynamic effects of intranasal live attenuated influenza vaccines (LAIV), such as the quadrivalent or trivalent formulations. This interaction may inhibit viral replication of the vaccine, potentially reducing its effectiveness. The use of baloxavir marboxil with intranasal LAIV has not been evaluated. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Ublituximab may reduce the efficacy of baloxavir marboxil due to its immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate and aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate also reduce the levels or efficacy of baloxavir marboxil through cation binding in the GI tract. Avoidance or substitution with an alternative drug is advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid co-administration or consider an alternative therapy. Calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, calcium gluconate, and calcium/vitamin D combinations all reduce the levels or efficacy of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoidance or substitution with an alternative drug is recommended. Carbonyl iron, chromium, citric acid/sodium bicarbonate, copper, ferric carboxymaltose, ferric citrate, ferric gluconate, ferric maltol, ferric pyrophosphate dialysate, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, ferrous sulfate, and ferumoxytol all decrease the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Iodine reduces the levels or efficacy of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoidance or substitution with an alternative drug is advised. Iron dextran complex and iron sucrose also decrease the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil through cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid co-administration or consider an alternative therapy.
